topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the learning objectives regarding environmental exposures and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: General Concepts and Epidemiology of Cancer Causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how genetic mutations, endogenous biological errors, and environmental exposures interact across global populations to drive cancer development.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote cancer, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing to form reactive DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental host contexts facilitate tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to identify and evaluate carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic risks against everyday benefits and offering final closing remarks.
